reasons: Tests exist for the standing, invalid resolution and collapsed helpers.
Only three of the six sections were provided, so the edge note and the field enumeration test could not be checked here.
No test run result was available to confirm they pass.

terms.meaning: a fixed, checked sample set of records used as the reference for correct output
the test runner that executes these checks
the label a claim gets, such as grounded, unsupported or declared prerequisite, based on its evidence

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test file setup
sections.what: Loads the test tool, the generated sample data, and the helper functions from the process and provenance views. It is the starting point that every test group relies on.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file comment. Loading the generated data lets the tests use real shapes.
sections.watch_out: If the generated file moves or is renamed, every test fails at this point.

sections.name: standingFor
sections.title: Tests for the standing rule
sections.what: Checks that a declared prerequisite with evidence gets its own standing, that one with no evidence falls back to unsupported, and that grounded and unsupported resolutions read from their citations.
sections.why: The comment explains that the empty case would show two contradictory statements on one claim, so it is tested directly.
sections.watch_out: These tests protect a rule the schema also enforces, so a change in one should be matched in the other.

sections.name: invalidResolutionNote
sections.title: Tests for the invalid resolution warning
sections.what: Checks that the warning appears for a declared prerequisite with no citations, with the expected words, and that it stays silent for the valid combinations.
sections.why: Likely reason: the warning is the page's only signal that a bad record got through, so both its presence and its silence are tested.
sections.watch_out: The test checks for specific warning words, so rewording the warning will break the test.

sections.name: edgeNoteFor
sections.title: Tests for prerequisite notes
sections.what: Checks the note shown for a prerequisite on a process page. A prerequisite that creates an edge should name the edge and its reason. A prerequisite with no matching edge should be said out loud. An untyped prerequisite should be named as untyped. Nothing should be returned when there is no reference to match.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page must not guess or quietly hide a broken dependency. The comment notes the missing-edge case never occurs on the golden set, so the test uses a sample list instead.
sections.watch_out: The missing-edge test depends on the sample edge list in this file, so changing that list can change what the test actually proves.

sections.name: collapsed
sections.title: Tests for reading collapsed fingerprints
sections.what: Checks the collapsed-fingerprint reader against a plain value, a collapsed value with a count, a digest that itself contains a colon, and an empty value. The expected outputs are exact, so any change in the shape of the result fails these tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: to pin down parsing behaviour, since an earlier version of the reader produced a wrong label. The reason is not stated in the code itself.
sections.watch_out: The expected values are exact, so a deliberate change to the reader's output must be paired with an update to these tests.

sections.name: the view enumerates every field the schema declares
sections.title: Checks that every schema field is shown
sections.what: Runs once per record to confirm the view displays every scorecard field and every parameter the schema declares. It also confirms there are exactly nine ordered dimensions, matching the caption on the page. A record with an unexpected field fails the test.
sections.why: The comment says the compile-time check catches a schema field the view does not list, while this runtime check catches a record carrying a field the schema does not declare. Each check fails on a different problem.
sections.watch_out: These tests use the real artifact bundle, so a failure may come from the data rather than from the view code. Check the record named in the test name first.

summary: Tests the small helper functions used by the process and provenance pages, including the branches that the sample data never reaches.
purpose: Makes sure the display rules for standing, invalid resolutions, wave-plan edges and collapsed digests behave correctly in every case.
why: The file comment says it covers the branches the golden data does not reach, so the rare cases are still tested.
how: Loads the generated artifacts and imports the helper functions from the process and provenance views. Each helper is checked in its own group of tests covering its valid and invalid inputs.
inputs: Hand-written test inputs for each helper, plus the generated artifacts file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner for each helper.
risks: The test file only checks some helpers. Only three of its six sections were available to read here, so the coverage of the rest is unknown.
debug: If a test fails, read the test name, then the helper it names in the view file. A mismatch in a warning string often means the wording was changed in one place and not the other.
